previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: A male patient with end-stage renal disease, status post kidney transplant with complications, and a history of coronary artery disease and recent subendocardial infarction, was admitted for acute periumbilical abdominal pain that occurred during hemodialysis. Concern for mesenteric ischemia prompted a CT angiogram, which revealed severe calcific atherosclerosis and narrowing of the superior mesenteric artery but no evidence of acute ischemia. His symptoms improved without intervention, and he completed a session of hemodialysis without recurrence of pain. The chest pain reported was evaluated and deemed non-acute. He was discharged in stable condition with instructions to continue medical management of vascular risk factors, adhere to his renal diet, and follow up with nephrology and cardiology.

Brief Hospital Course:
___ with PMH CAD s/p multiple RCA PCIs, ESRD on HD with failed 
kidney transplant ___, HTN, ILD, gout, recent admissions for 
ischemic colitis (___) and pneumonia (___), now 
presenting with diarrhea.

# Gastroenteritis - Patient reported numerous episodes of watery 
diarrhea for two days prior to admission. C. diff infection was 
suspected as patient was recently on vanc and meropenem and was 
hospitalized. Patient was treated with PO flagyl until his C. 
diff toxin PCR came back negative. His diarrhea also resolved 
less 12 hours after presenting to the hospital. Due to the time 
course and clincal history, the patient likely had a viral 
gastroenteritis, and was not discharged on antibiotics. Patient 
is to follow-up with gastroenterology as an outpatient for a 
possible colonoscopy as he was recently admitted for possible 
ischemic colitis and now had another episode of diarrhea. 

# Ischemic colitis - Patient was recently discharged on ___ 
for ischemic colitis likely due to overaggressive fluid removal 
during dialysis. On CT of the abdomen and pelvis performed in 
the ED, the ascending colon at the hepatic flexure appeared 
mildly thick walled with mild pericolonic fat stranding, which 
could be due to colitis, possibly acute on chronic. However, his 
symptoms of nausea/vomiting/diarrhea along with abdominal pain 
which resolved was more consistent with gastroenteritis. 

# Hypertension: continued home metoprolol and isosorbide. 
Patient's amlodipine 5mg was discontinued as his blood pressures 
had been running low during dialysis.

COMPARISON:  CT abdomen pelvis on ___.

FINDINGS: 

Lungs and Heart: There is a small left-sided pleural effusion.  Additionally,
there is minimal bibasilar atelectasis.  There is no pneumothorax. There are
marked coronary artery calcifications.

Liver, Gallbladder: The liver is normal in size. There is no intra or
extrahepatic biliary ductal dilatation.  There is no evidence of pneumobilia. 
The gallbladder is distended but otherwise normal appearing.

Spleen: The spleen is normal in size.  There is significant calcified
atherosclerosis of the splenic artery.

Pancreas: The pancreas is unremarkable. There is no peripancreatic fat
stranding.

Kidneys, Adrenals: The native kidneys are atrophic. The renal graft in the
right lower pelvis is atrophied, but unchanged in appearance.  The adrenal
glands are normal bilaterally.

Bowel: The small bowel is grossly unremarkable and there is no evidence of
small bowel obstruction.  A duodenal diverticulum (series 2, image 30) is
again seen. The hepatic flexure of the ascending colon appears mildly thick
walled with possible subtle haziness of the adjacent fat.  There are areas
where there appear to be fatty infiltration of the submucosa, which may
indicate an acute on chronic process.  Again seen are multiple diverticula
throughout the descending colon and sigmoid colon however there is no evidence
of acute diverticulitis. The appendix is normal.  There is no free fluid or
free air in the abdomen.

Vessels: There is heavy, extensive calcification of the abdominal aorta.  As
well as dense calcifications at the origin of the celiac artery and bilateral
renal arteries. There is no aneurysmal dilatation of the abdominal aorta.

Lymph Nodes: There are no pathologically enlarged lymph nodes in the abdomen
or pelvis by CT size criteria.

Pelvis: Again seen is minimal bladder wall thickening as well as intermediate
density fluid within bladder. There is no evidence of pelvic sidewall
lymphadenopathy.

Osseous Structures: There are no suspicious lytic or blastic lesions seen in
the visualized osseous structures.
